boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Connecticut College
boards.description: An under-21-safe guide to the late-night dining and study spots that define the student experience at Connecticut College in New London.

cards.title: Oasis Snack Shop
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Hub in Crozier-Williams
cards.notes: Visit the first floor of 'Cro' for made-to-order burgers, fries, and sushi. It is a primary social hub for students seeking a study break or a late meal.
cards.short_summary: A central student hangout in the College Center offering diverse grill and grab-and-go options late into the evening.
cards.evidence_claim: Oasis is located on the first floor of Crozier-Williams and is described as a late-night hangout spot for students with made-to-order meals.
cards.access_notes: Open late during the academic semester; check CamelWeb for specific nightly hours.

cards.title: Coffee Grounds
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Cafe in Katharine Blunt House
cards.notes: Stop by for organic fair-trade coffee and homemade baked goods. This student-managed space often hosts open mics and club events until 10 PM.
cards.short_summary: A sustainable, student-run coffee shop located in KB House that serves as a vibrant evening community and performance space.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffee Grounds is open Monday through Thursday and Sunday until 10:00 PM.
cards.access_notes: Open until 10 PM Sunday-Thursday during the academic year.

cards.title: Shain Library
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Study Space
cards.notes: Utilize the first-floor cafe area for all-night study sessions. The library provides a robust wireless network and plenty of outlets for late-night productivity.
cards.short_summary: The campus's main library features a first-floor area that serves as a 24-hour study space for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Camel Café area in Shain Library doubles as a 24-hour study space.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: The first-floor cafe area is accessible 24 hours a day for student study.

cards.title: Harris Refectory
cards.subtitle: Main Dining Hall Late Hours
cards.notes: Head to the Plex for late-night dining options on select evenings. The Social House at Harris offers pizza, grill items, and a dedicated vegetarian station.
cards.short_summary: The college's primary dining hall, recently transformed into the Social House, offering evening meal service for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Harris Refectory (Social House) offers dinner and has been noted for late-night dining availability until 10 PM on Sundays.
cards.access_notes: Regular dinner until 7:15 PM; check CamelWeb for specific late-night dining dates and extended hours.

cards.title: 7-Eleven
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Convenience on Broad Street
cards.notes: Walk or drive down to Broad Street for 24-hour access to snacks, drinks, and basic essentials. It is a reliable off-campus stop for late-night needs.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour convenience store located near campus providing round-the-clock access to food and supplies.
cards.evidence_claim: The 7-Eleven at 283 Broad Street in New London is open 24/7.
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Diner Classics
cards.notes: Gather a group for a late-night Grand Slam or milkshake. This diner is open 24/7 and is a classic destination for students after evening events.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner located on South Frontage Road offering a full breakfast, lunch, and dinner menu at any hour.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny's at 322 S Frontage Road in New London is open 24 hours.
cards.source_title: Denny's 322 S FRONTAGE ROAD I-95 RESTAURANT
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily.

cards.title: Domino's Pizza
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Delivery Staple
cards.notes: Order pizza, wings, or cheesy bread for delivery directly to your residence hall. They serve the campus community well past midnight on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A popular late-night delivery option for students, offering a full menu of pizza and sides until the early morning hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Domino's at 938 Bank Street is open until 1:00 AM or later for delivery and carryout.
cards.source_title: 938 Bank Street in New London - Domino's Pizza
cards.access_notes: Open until 1 AM daily, with extended hours on Friday and Saturday.

cards.title: CVS Pharmacy
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Essentials on Bank St
cards.notes: Pick up snacks, beverages, or health supplies until 9 PM. While not 24 hours, it is a key stop for students before the late-night study grind begins.
cards.short_summary: A conveniently located pharmacy and convenience store on Bank Street for evening supplies and snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The CVS at 817 Bank Street is open until 9:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: CVS Pharmacy at 817 Bank Street New London, CT 06320
cards.access_notes: Open until 9 PM daily.

cards.title: McDonald's
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Drive-Thru
cards.notes: Swing through the drive-thru for a quick late-night meal. Located on Colman Street, it is a frequent stop for students with access to a car.
cards.short_summary: A classic fast-food option with late-night drive-thru service located a short drive from the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The McDonald's at 406 Colman Street offers late-night hours and drive-thru service.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru typically open late; check the app for current nightly closing times.

cards.title: Ruane's Den
cards.subtitle: South Campus Coffee Spot
cards.notes: Visit the Walk-In Coffee Closet for a caffeine boost on South Campus. This student-run spot in Harkness House provides a cozy evening atmosphere for studying.
cards.short_summary: A student-managed coffee shop located in Harkness Residence Hall, serving the south end of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruane's Den is a student-run cafe located in Harkness House and is part of the Conn Coffee organization.
cards.access_notes: Open during the academic year; check CamelWeb for current student-staffed hours.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the student-led hubs, late-night study nooks, and quiet natural retreats that define daily life at Connecticut College beyond the official tour path.

cards.title: The MOBROC Barn
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Music Practice Space
cards.notes: Practice or watch student bands in this converted squash court. It features a full sound system and a second-level balcony for viewing live rehearsals.
cards.short_summary: A student-run music practice and performance venue managed by Musicians Organized for Bands Rights on Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Barn (or MOBROC Barn) is a student-run practice and performance space in a converted squash court with a sound system and balcony.
cards.access_notes: Primarily used by MOBROC member bands for practice and scheduled student performances.

cards.title: Coffee Grounds
cards.subtitle: Student-Run Café in Katharine Blunt House
cards.notes: Visit this cozy, student-managed coffee shop for a quiet study session. It is known for its relaxed atmosphere and is located inside the KB residence hall.
cards.short_summary: A popular student-run café located on the first floor of Katharine Blunt House, offering a social study environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Coffee Grounds is a student-run coffee shop located in Katharine Blunt House.
cards.access_notes: Open to the campus community; hours are typically posted at the entrance and managed by student staff.

cards.title: Blue Camel Café
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour Study Space in Shain Library
cards.notes: Utilize this first-floor café area for late-night cramming. While the counter closes, the seating area remains accessible 24/7 for students with ID.
cards.short_summary: A central campus café that doubles as a 24-hour study lounge for students within the Charles E. Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Camel Café is located on the first floor of Shain Library and doubles as a 24-hour study space.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: The seating area is accessible 24 hours a day for students with a valid Camel Card.

cards.title: Unity House Kitchen
cards.subtitle: Communal Cooking and Gathering Space
cards.notes: Prepare a meal with friends in this fully equipped kitchen. It serves as a central social hub for students of all backgrounds to share food and culture.
cards.short_summary: A communal kitchen and lounge area within the Unity House multicultural center used for student gatherings and meal preparation.
cards.evidence_claim: Unity House features a kitchen available for campus community members to prepare meals and host events.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours (typically 8:30 am to 10:00 pm) for student use.

cards.title: Ruane's Den
cards.subtitle: Walk-In Coffee Closet in Harkness House
cards.notes: Find a quiet corner in this south campus coffee shop. It features big-screen TVs and comfortable seating, making it ideal for group meetings or solo study.
cards.short_summary: A student-run coffee shop and social space located on the first floor of Harkness Residence Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Ruane's Den is a student-run café location in Harkness Residence Hall with comfy seating and big-screen TVs.
cards.access_notes: Located within a residence hall; accessible to the college community during operating hours.

cards.title: The Granite Classroom
cards.subtitle: Outdoor Learning Space on Tempel Green
cards.notes: Attend a class or study outdoors at this granite-fashioned classroom. It offers expansive views of the Long Island Sound and the Thames River.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor classroom made of granite located on Tempel Green, used for both formal instruction and informal student study.
cards.evidence_claim: Tempel Green features an outdoor classroom fashioned from granite where some professors move their classes.
cards.access_notes: Open public space on the main campus green; available for use when not occupied by a scheduled class.

cards.title: Caroline Black Garden
cards.subtitle: Quiet Arboretum Retreat
cards.notes: Escape the campus bustle in this 4-acre garden. It is a favorite spot for students seeking a peaceful environment for reflection or quiet reading.
cards.short_summary: A diverse botanical collection within the Arboretum, serving as a tranquil space for recreation and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Caroline Black Garden is a 4-acre part of the Arboretum used for recreation and reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public from sunrise to sunset, 365 days a year.

cards.title: Hillel House Great Room
cards.subtitle: Study and Social Space
cards.notes: Study in the Great Room or relax on the couches downstairs. This space offers a quiet library and a welcoming atmosphere for students of all faiths.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose space within the Zachs Hillel House used for studying, lectures, and community dinners.
cards.evidence_claim: Zachs Hillel House features a great room for studying, lectures, and dinners, plus a library and downstairs lounge with comfy chairs.
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; building hours typically follow standard campus facility schedules.

cards.title: The White Box Gallery
cards.subtitle: Student Exhibition Space
cards.notes: View rotating student work in this dedicated exhibition space. It provides a professional-style gallery setting for course projects and senior thesis work.
cards.short_summary: A modern exhibition space within the Cummings Arts Center specifically for student art displays and special projects.
cards.evidence_claim: The Cummings Arts Center houses a white-box gallery for student exhibitions and special course projects.
cards.access_notes: Open during Cummings Arts Center building hours; exhibitions change periodically throughout the semester.

cards.title: Harkness Chapel Library
cards.subtitle: Quiet Lower-Level Study Nook
cards.notes: Discover this secluded library on the lower level of the chapel. It is one of the quietest spots on campus for focused reading and research.
cards.short_summary: A small, quiet library and meeting area located in the lower level of the historic Harkness Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: In the lower level of Harkness Chapel are offices, meeting rooms, and a library.
cards.access_notes: Accessible during chapel building hours; check the online calendar for event-related closures.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Connecticut College, from expansive arboretum trails to student-run performance venues and art galleries.

cards.title: Stroll the Native Plant Collection
cards.subtitle: Connecticut College Arboretum
cards.notes: Walk through 25 acres of woody plants and wildflowers. Use the Williams Street entrance to access easy walking paths and the four-acre pond for a quiet outdoor break.
cards.short_summary: A 25-acre collection of native trees and shrubs featuring easy walking trails and a central pond.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum is free and open to the public sunrise to sunset, 365 days a year.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Free street parking is available at the Williams Street entrance.

cards.title: Relax on Tempel Green
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Commons
cards.notes: Gather for a picnic or group study session on this expansive lawn. It offers sweeping views of the Long Island Sound and features an outdoor classroom made of granite.
cards.short_summary: The central campus green used for social gatherings, picnics, and outdoor studying with water views.
cards.evidence_claim: Tempel Green, which offers sweeping views of Long Island Sound, is a favorite place to study and relax.
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space; most active during daylight hours in warmer months.

cards.title: Explore the Lyman Allyn
cards.subtitle: South Campus Art Museum
cards.notes: Browse permanent collections and rotating exhibitions. Students and staff at Connecticut College receive free general admission to the galleries and outdoor sculpture trail.
cards.short_summary: An art museum located at the south end of campus featuring over 17,000 objects and a sculpture trail.
cards.evidence_claim: Students and staff at Connecticut College receive free general admission.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission - Lyman Allyn Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Saturday 10am-5pm and Sunday 1pm-5pm. Closed Mondays.

cards.title: Study in Shain Library
cards.subtitle: Campus Research Hub
cards.notes: Utilize collaborative study areas and whiteboards for group work. The first floor is a social, non-quiet space ideal for meeting classmates near the Blue Camel Cafe.
cards.short_summary: The main campus library offering diverse study environments from social lounges to quiet research floors.
cards.evidence_claim: Shain Library features classrooms and collaborative study areas... the first floor is traditionally not a quiet space.
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; check website for specific late-night hours for students.

cards.title: Visit the Cummings Gallery
cards.subtitle: Cummings Arts Center
cards.notes: View faculty and student-curated exhibitions in this on-campus gallery. It is free and open to the public, showcasing diverse media from sculpture to digital art.
cards.short_summary: A professional gallery space within the Cummings Arts Center hosting rotating contemporary art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Joanne Toor Cummings Gallery, located in Cummings Arts Center, is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours are typically Monday-Friday 9am-5pm and Saturday-Sunday 1pm-4pm.

cards.title: Attend a Chapel Performance
cards.subtitle: Historic Performance Venue
cards.notes: Listen to a cappella concerts or student recitals in this non-denominational space. The chapel is known for its superb acoustics and quintessential campus silhouette.
cards.short_summary: A historic 400-seat chapel used for religious services, musical performances, and guest lectures.
cards.evidence_claim: Harkness Chapel hosts a variety of musical performances each year, including a cappella concerts and student recitals.
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled events and services; check the campus calendar for public performance dates.

cards.title: Hike Mamacoke Island
cards.subtitle: Arboretum Natural Area
cards.notes: Trek through this 40-acre rocky island attached by a tidal salt marsh. It is a designated Important Bird Area, perfect for winter duck watching and nature photography.
cards.short_summary: A rugged natural area within the Arboretum offering hiking trails and bird-watching opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: Mamacoke Island... is a designated natural area within the Connecticut College Arboretum... open to the public free of charge.
cards.access_notes: Accessible via the Arboretum; check tide charts as the marsh crossing is best at low tide.

cards.title: Hang Out in Cro Pit
cards.subtitle: Crozier-Williams Student Center
cards.notes: Meet friends in the heart of campus activity. This central lounge area in 'Cro' is the hub for student clubs, mail services, and casual social interaction.
cards.short_summary: The primary social lounge and activity hub located within the Crozier-Williams College Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Located in the center of campus, the College Center at Crozier-Williams... is home to Cro Pit... the heart of campus activity.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; primary student hub with late-night access for residents.

cards.title: Visit Caroline Black Garden
cards.subtitle: Landscaped Arboretum Collection
cards.notes: Explore a diverse collection of ornamental trees and shrubs across from the main campus. This garden features a small stream and mature conifers for a peaceful retreat.
cards.short_summary: A four-acre landscaped garden showcasing diverse plant species for landscaping and aesthetic enjoyment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Caroline Black Garden... is open to the public every day of the year from sunrise to sunset. General admission is free.
cards.access_notes: Located off Route 32; parking is available behind Vinal Cottage.

cards.title: Rock Out at the Barn
cards.subtitle: Student Music Space
cards.notes: Watch student bands practice or perform in this converted squash court. It features a full sound system and a second-level balcony for spectators.
cards.short_summary: A student-run music practice and performance venue managed by Musicians Organized for Bands Rights on Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: MOBROC Barn... provides bands with access to this practice and performance space... a converted squash court.
cards.access_notes: Primarily a student-use space; performances are often open to the campus community.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.entity_name: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room
cards.title: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, First Floor
cards.notes: Study in a serene environment surrounded by Chinese scrolls and Asian art. This quiet reading area features comfortable armchairs and large windows for natural light.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, art-filled reading room on the main floor of Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room serves as both a quiet reading area and a permanent exhibition space for Asian art.
cards.source_title: Charles Chu Asian Art Reading Room - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open during Shain Library hours; typically accessible to students for quiet study.

cards.title: Blue Camel Café
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, First Floor
cards.notes: Utilize this 24-hour study space for late-night sessions. The cafe offers specialty coffees and snacks in a social atmosphere with both indoor and outdoor seating.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour study space and coffee shop located within Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Blue Camel Café is located in a prominent first-floor spot and doubles as a 24-hour study space.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: The cafe space is available for 24-hour study for students with campus access.

cards.title: Shain Library Collaboration Rooms
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, Multiple Floors
cards.notes: Reserve one of ten group rooms equipped with whiteboard walls and LCD panels. These spaces are ideal for team projects and can be booked online via LibCal.
cards.short_summary: Ten reservable group study rooms with digital displays and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: Ten reservable collaboration rooms, each outfitted with whiteboard walls and LCD panels on which students can share laptop displays.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Reservations are required through the library's online booking system.

cards.title: Greer Music Library
cards.subtitle: Cummings Arts Center, Lower Level
cards.notes: Find a quiet nook or reading table among 20,000 recordings and scores. This specialized library offers a traditional atmosphere for focused academic work.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized library for music research and study in Cummings Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: A comfortable reading area, tables and nooks provide library users with a variety of spaces for both quiet and collaborative study.
cards.access_notes: Open during posted music library hours; accessible to all students.

cards.title: Blaustein Humanities Center Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Blaustein Humanities Center
cards.notes: Study at the large tables or lounge chairs in the wings of the third floor. This area is known for its calm atmosphere and proximity to campus coffee shops.
cards.short_summary: A quiet study area with tables and couches on the top floor of Blaustein.
cards.evidence_claim: Blaustein is a criminally underrated place to get work done... the cozy tables in the third floor wings.
cards.source_title: New Camels, Find Your On-Campus Oasis! | The College Voice
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; typically quietest during non-class times.

cards.title: New London Hall Classrooms
cards.subtitle: New London Hall
cards.notes: Gather for group study in these modern life sciences classrooms. The building features large windows with campus views and state-of-the-art facilities.
cards.short_summary: Modern classrooms in the life sciences building used for group study.
cards.evidence_claim: One of the best places to study as a group on campus is New London Hall... we have taken one of the classrooms and worked at the desks together.
cards.source_title: Our Favorite Study Spots On Campus - Her Campus
cards.access_notes: Available for study when classes are not in session; building access required.

cards.title: Tempel Green Outdoor Classroom
cards.subtitle: Tempel Green
cards.notes: Study outdoors at the granite-fashioned classroom on the green. This spot offers views of Long Island Sound and is popular for group sessions in warmer months.
cards.short_summary: A granite outdoor classroom located on the main campus green.
cards.evidence_claim: Some professors move their classes to Tempel Green, which features an outdoor classroom fashioned from granite.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7; best used during daylight hours in fair weather.

cards.title: Zachs Hillel House Great Room
cards.subtitle: Zachs Hillel House
cards.notes: Work in the Great Room, which is designed for studying, lectures, and dinners. The house also features a library and comfortable lounge seating for students.
cards.short_summary: A multi-purpose study and community space within the Zachs Hillel House.
cards.evidence_claim: The building features a kosher kitchen; a great room for studying, lectures and dinners; a library; conference room; and office space.
cards.access_notes: Accessible to the campus community; check for scheduled events.

cards.title: Crozier-Williams Student Lounge
cards.subtitle: College Center at Crozier-Williams
cards.notes: Find a spot in the heart of campus activity at 'Cro.' The center offers various lounge areas and collaborative spaces near student organization offices.
cards.short_summary: Central campus center lounge areas for social and informal study.
cards.evidence_claim: A renovated Cro... can fully realize its potential as a space that brings faculty, staff and students together for formal, informal and coincidental interactions.
cards.access_notes: Open during building hours; typically high-traffic and social.

cards.title: Technology Commons
cards.subtitle: Shain Library, Lower Level
cards.notes: Access high-performance workstations and the Visualization Wall. This lower-level space is designed for digital projects and collaborative tech-heavy work.
cards.short_summary: A tech-focused collaborative study space on the lower level of Shain Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Lower-level spaces include the Technology Commons, providing an array of seating for group work; an Advanced Workstation Cluster... and the Visualization Wall.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open during Shain Library hours; specialized software available on workstations.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Connecticut College, from the historic waterfront to the neighborhood hubs of New London.

cards.title: Williams Street
cards.subtitle: Williams Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this casual neighborhood staple for grinders and pizza. It is a frequent off-campus dining choice for students living in the nearby Winchester Road apartments.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining landmark on the Williams Street corridor known for its grinders and proximity to student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Mr. G's Restaurant is located at 452 Williams Street and is cited as a friendly, casual dining spot for the college community.
cards.access_notes: Open daily for lunch and dinner; accessible via a short walk or drive from the southern campus entrance.

cards.title: Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Waterfront District
cards.notes: Stop by this historic cafe for their signature 'Love Salad' or a coffee. The deck offers views of the Thames River and is a popular weekend destination for students.
cards.short_summary: A historic Bank Street cafe famous for its river views and signature dishes, serving as a central downtown hangout.
cards.evidence_claim: Muddy Waters Cafe is located at 40 Bank Street and is described as a popular downtown stop for students.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Located in the heart of the downtown historic district.

cards.title: State Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown State Street District
cards.notes: View this restored historic building that has served as a residential hub for upperclassmen. It anchors the top of the State Street commercial corridor.
cards.short_summary: A prominent historic building on State Street that has integrated college residential life with the downtown community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Manwaring Building at 225 State Street has been used for Connecticut College student housing in downtown New London.
cards.source_title: Downtown New London building to house Conn College students
cards.access_notes: The building is a private residence; the exterior is a landmark of the State Street district.

cards.title: Hodges Square
cards.subtitle: Hodges Square Village
cards.notes: Explore this community space designed and built by Conn architecture and psychology students. It serves as a focal point for neighborhood revitalization efforts.
cards.short_summary: A student-designed public parklet that represents the college's active role in revitalizing the Hodges Square neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hodges Square Parklet was a design-build project by Connecticut College students to revitalize the local business district.
cards.source_title: Camels Add Charm to Hodges Square - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space located approximately one mile from the main campus.

cards.title: Washington Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Arts District
cards.notes: Visit for breakfast or lunch in a space known for its community vibe. It is a frequent Sunday morning destination for students seeking a quiet off-campus study spot.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown coffee house and bakery known for its welcoming atmosphere and student-friendly environment.
cards.evidence_claim: Washington Street Coffee House is located at 13 Washington Street and is a staple for students in downtown New London.
cards.source_title: FOOD MENU - Washington Street Coffee House
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM.

cards.title: Huntington Street
cards.subtitle: Huntington Street Historic Area
cards.notes: Dine at this long-standing Italian restaurant located at the corner of Huntington and Broad. It is a classic choice for visiting families and special occasions.
cards.short_summary: A rustic Italian favorite on Huntington Street, serving the New London community since 1999.
cards.evidence_claim: Tony D's is located at 92 Huntington Street and is a recommended dining destination for the college community.
cards.access_notes: Open for lunch and dinner; reservations are often recommended for weekend dining.

cards.title: Williams Street
cards.subtitle: Upper Williams Street
cards.notes: Explore American art and local history at this museum adjacent to campus. Admission is free for Connecticut College students and staff.
cards.short_summary: A world-class art museum located on the edge of campus, offering free access to the college community.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lyman Allyn Art Museum is located at 625 Williams Street and offers free admission to Connecticut College students.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission - Lyman Allyn Art Museum
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday through Saturday 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM, and Sunday 1:00 PM - 5:00 PM.

cards.title: Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Arts District
cards.notes: Visit this non-profit arts cooperative and its outdoor Art Park. It hosts year-round exhibitions and performances that are central to New London's cultural scene.
cards.short_summary: A landmark arts center on Bank Street featuring galleries and an outdoor amphitheater for community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Hygienic Art is located at 79-83 Bank Street and serves as a major destination for art and performances in New London.
cards.access_notes: Galleries are open to the public; the Art Park hosts seasonal outdoor events.

cards.title: Montauk Avenue
cards.subtitle: Mitchell College Area
cards.notes: Enjoy ice cream at this seasonal parlor that has been a local tradition for over 80 years. It is a popular destination for students during the warmer months.
cards.short_summary: A historic seasonal ice cream parlor on Montauk Avenue that serves as a community gathering spot.
cards.evidence_claim: Michael's Dairy is located at 629 Montauk Avenue and is a well-known local ice cream destination.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from April 1 to October 30, 12:00 PM to 9:00 PM.

cards.title: Bank Street
cards.subtitle: Downtown Waterfront District
cards.notes: Stop by this convenience market for sandwiches and snacks. It is a key resource for students living in or visiting the downtown residential area.
cards.short_summary: A local market on Bank Street providing essential groceries and prepared foods to the downtown student population.
cards.evidence_claim: Honey Bee Farms is located at 298 Bank Street and is a frequent stop for students in the downtown area.
cards.source_title: Conn College students bring positivity to downtown New London
cards.access_notes: Open daily; centrally located near the downtown waterfront.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Discover the unique rituals and annual celebrations that define the Camel experience at Connecticut College, from spring music festivals to symbolic saplings.

cards.title: Floralia
cards.subtitle: The Premier Spring Music Festival
cards.notes: Join the day-long celebration in May featuring live bands and dancing at the Shain Library Amphitheater.
cards.short_summary: A student-founded spring music festival held annually since 1977 at the Shain Library Amphitheater.
cards.evidence_claim: Floralia is Connecticut College's one-day student spring festival held every year in May, known for live music and dancing in the Shain Library Amphitheatre.
cards.access_notes: Held annually in May; primarily for students and registered alumni.

cards.title: The Sapling Tradition
cards.subtitle: A Growing Connection to Campus
cards.notes: Carry a White Spruce sapling during Commencement to symbolize your lifelong connection to the college.
cards.short_summary: Graduates receive tree saplings at Commencement, a tradition representing the college seal and environmental stewardship.
cards.evidence_claim: Connecticut College graduates are presented with White Spruce saplings which they carry as they march at Commencement, a tradition started with the Class of 1993.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the annual Commencement ceremony for graduating seniors.

cards.title: Moonlight Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Finals Fuel
cards.notes: Enjoy breakfast served by college administrators at Harris Refectory to kick off the first semester's final exams.
cards.short_summary: A late-night study break where staff serve breakfast to students to mark the start of finals week.
cards.evidence_claim: Moonlight Breakfast is an annual late-night study break where campus administrators serve breakfast to students at the start of final exams.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during finals week in the Harris Refectory.

cards.title: Harvestfest
cards.subtitle: Fall Carnival on the Green
cards.notes: Browse over 70 student club booths selling treats and Camel gear during this outdoor autumn festival.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor carnival featuring food and entertainment, held during Fall Weekend on the campus greens.
cards.evidence_claim: Harvestfest is an outdoor carnival/festival with food and entertainment, usually held in conjunction with Fall Weekend.
cards.access_notes: Open to students, families, and alumni during Fall Weekend in October.

cards.title: Camelympics
cards.subtitle: Inter-House Spirit Competition
cards.notes: Represent your residence house in competitions ranging from volleyball to board games to win the campus spirit title.
cards.short_summary: A residence house competition featuring athletic and social events to promote community spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Camelympics is a tradition that pits residence houses against one another in friendly competition, including events like volleyball and Quidditch.
cards.access_notes: Annual event for residential students; locations vary across campus.

cards.title: Founders Day Bell Ringing
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the College Charter
cards.notes: Listen for the Harkness Chapel bell ringing at noon every April 5th to mark the college's official birthday.
cards.short_summary: An annual celebration on April 5th featuring a ceremonial bell ringing and birthday cake to honor the college's 1911 founding.
cards.evidence_claim: Founders Day is celebrated on April 5, featuring a ceremonial bell-ringing at noon and birthday cake in Harris Refectory.
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on April 5th at Harkness Chapel and Harris Refectory.

cards.title: The Laurel Chain
cards.subtitle: A Processional of Honor
cards.notes: Watch junior and sophomore students carry chains of laurel to guide the graduating class to their ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A commencement tradition where underclassmen carry laurel chains to honor the graduating seniors.
cards.evidence_claim: The laurel chain has been part of ceremonies since 1919; members of the junior and sophomore classes carry chains of laurel to guide graduates.
cards.access_notes: Performed during the annual Commencement processional.

cards.title: Matriculation Pledge
cards.subtitle: Commitment to the Honor Code
cards.notes: Formally join the college community by signing the pledge to uphold integrity and civility during Convocation.
cards.short_summary: New students formally sign the Honor Code pledge during the opening Convocation ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: When students matriculate, they pledge to adhere to the Connecticut College Honor Code by formally signing the matriculation pledge during Convocation.
cards.access_notes: Required for all incoming first-year students during orientation.

cards.title: Festivus
cards.subtitle: A Winter Festival for All
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of the fall semester with a non-denominational party featuring music and winter activities.
cards.short_summary: An annual winter holiday party held at the end of the fall semester as an alternative to traditional celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Festivus is the annual non-denominational holiday party typically hosted in the Crozier-Williams Student Center at the end of the fall semester.
cards.source_title: Festivus Returns to Conn - The College Voice
cards.access_notes: Held in December at the Crozier-Williams Student Center.

cards.title: Class Banner Presentation
cards.subtitle: Four Colors of Community
cards.notes: Receive your class year's banner in one of four rotating color schemes during the Convocation ceremony.
cards.short_summary: The Alumni Association presents a colored banner to the incoming class, which follows them through graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Each year, the Alumni Association bestows on the incoming class a banner bearing their graduation year in one of four rotating color schemes.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during the Convocation ceremony for new students.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Connecticut College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Navigate your first days as a Camel with this sequence of essential orientation stops, from move-in at Crozier-Williams to the final picnic on Tempel Green.

cards.title: Check-in at Cro
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Start your journey at 'Cro' to pick up your room keys and orientation materials. The mailroom is also here if you shipped packages ahead of time.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for move-in day check-in and initial student resources.
cards.evidence_claim: First-year students check in at Crozier-Williams before moving into residence halls, and the mailroom is located on the first floor.
cards.access_notes: Open for check-in during assigned morning time slots (typically 8-11 AM).

cards.title: First Meal at Harris
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Lunch
cards.notes: Head to the Social House at Harris for your first meal on campus. It is the largest dining hall and a primary spot for meeting your new floor mates.
cards.short_summary: The main campus dining hall where students gather for community meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Harris Refectory is the College's largest dining hall and serves as a central location for student meals.
cards.source_title: Financial Aid, Housing, Orientation - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Accessible via student Camel Card; check CamelWeb for specific orientation hours.

cards.title: New Student Welcome
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Afternoon
cards.notes: Gather in this historic venue for the official welcome from the Dean of First-Year Students and an overview of your orientation schedule.
cards.short_summary: A major performance venue used for the official orientation welcome ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: New students gather in Palmer Auditorium for a New Student Welcome session on Arrival Day afternoon.
cards.source_title: Conn welcomes Class of 2029 - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Mandatory attendance for all new students during the scheduled welcome session.

cards.title: Meet Your Seminar Group
cards.subtitle: Wednesday Late Afternoon
cards.notes: Find your assigned color group on the green to meet your student advisers and first-year seminar peers for the first time.
cards.short_summary: The central campus lawn used for orientation group meetings and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Students gather with their first-year seminar groups on Tempel Green during orientation.
cards.source_title: Conn welcomes Class of 2029 - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor space; look for student advisers holding color-coded signs.

cards.title: Batch Blast Social
cards.subtitle: Thursday Evening
cards.notes: Enjoy a night of comedy, hypnotists, or live music. This long-standing tradition is designed specifically to help first-years bond.
cards.short_summary: An annual social event for first-year students featuring entertainment and picnics.
cards.evidence_claim: Batch Blast takes place in August for first-year students and includes social events like comedy acts and hypnotists.
cards.access_notes: Exclusive to first-year students as part of Welcome Weekend programming.

cards.title: Explore the Arbo
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning
cards.notes: Take a break from sessions with a walk through the 750-acre 'living laboratory.' The Native Plant Collection is a student favorite for quiet reflection.
cards.short_summary: A vast botanical garden and natural area integrated into the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Arboretum offers 750 acres of managed landscapes and natural areas for recreation and reflection.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset; main entrance is on Williams Street.

cards.title: Library Tech Tour
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon
cards.notes: Visit the Technology Commons to see the Visualization Wall and find your favorite study nook before classes begin on Tuesday.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus library featuring advanced digital scholarship tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Shain Library features a Technology Commons with a Visualization Wall and is open for student use before classes start.
cards.source_title: Charles E. Shain Library - Connecticut College
cards.access_notes: Open 8:00 AM to midnight on the Monday before classes start; check site for weekend hours.

cards.title: Harkness Chapel Visit
cards.subtitle: Saturday Morning
cards.notes: Step inside this colonial-style chapel for a moment of quiet or to appreciate the acoustics. It often hosts student recitals and community events.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus chapel used for religious services and musical performances.
cards.evidence_claim: Harkness Chapel is used for religious services, special events, and musical performances like a cappella concerts.
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled services and public events; check the online calendar for access.

cards.title: New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Monday Morning
cards.notes: Join the formal opening of the academic year. This ceremony introduces the Honor Code and officially welcomes you into the Camel community.
cards.short_summary: The formal ceremony marking the beginning of the academic year for new students.
cards.evidence_claim: Convocation celebrates the formal opening of the academic year and welcomes new students, highlighting the Honor Code.
cards.access_notes: Mandatory for all new students; typically held on the Monday before classes begin.

cards.title: All-Campus Picnic
cards.subtitle: Monday Lunch
cards.notes: Celebrate the end of orientation with a community-wide picnic on the green immediately following Convocation. Classes start tomorrow!
cards.short_summary: A celebratory outdoor meal for the entire campus community after Convocation.
cards.evidence_claim: Immediately following Convocation, the campus community gathers for an all-campus picnic.
cards.access_notes: Held on Tempel Green; open to all students, faculty, and staff.
